title: Old-Time Sweet Potato Storage
subtitle: Tips From a 1918 USDA Bulletin
desc: Old-time sweet potato storage tips from USDA Farmers' Bulletin 970 (1918), updated for today: dig before frost, handle gently, cure warm and humid for about 10 days, then store at 55–60°F and never let them chill below 50°F so they keep sweet all winter.

title: How to Pressure Can Carrots
subtitle: USDA Tested Method
desc: How to can carrots safely in a pressure canner, following the USDA Complete Guide to Home Canning: raw or hot pack, 1-inch headspace, 25 minutes for pints and 30 for quarts at 10 lb (weighted gauge, 0–1,000 ft) or 11 lb (dial gauge); adjust pressure for altitude. Carrots are low-acid, so never water bath them.

title: Freeze Thanksgiving Leftovers
subtitle: Safe Turkey Storage Tips
desc: How to store and freeze Thanksgiving turkey leftovers safely: refrigerate within 2 hours, slice meat off the bone into shallow containers, eat refrigerated leftovers within 3–4 days or freeze them for best quality within 2–6 months, and reheat to 165°F.

title: Freezer Food in a Power Outage
subtitle: What to Keep, What to Toss
desc: What to do with freezer food in a power outage: keep the door shut, a full freezer stays cold about 48 hours and a half-full one about 24, and food that still has ice crystals or is at 40°F or below can be safely refrozen. Winter storm preparedness for the homestead pantry.

title: How to Store Seeds Over Winter
subtitle: Keep Them Ready for Spring
desc: How to store vegetable seeds over winter: dry them fully, seal them in an airtight jar with a silica gel packet, keep them cool, dark and dry (the fridge works), label with variety and year, and do a quick paper-towel germination test before spring planting.
